A focus detection device includes: a plurality of micro-lenses at which light fluxes through an image forming optical system enter, disposed in a two-dimensional array pattern; a plurality of light receiving elements disposed in correspondence to each of the plurality of micro-lenses; a focus detection unit that executes a detection of a defocus quantity of the image forming optical system by detecting, based upon outputs from the plurality of light receiving elements, a phase difference of a plurality of light fluxes through different areas of the image forming optical system; and a recognition unit that recognizes, based upon the outputs from the plurality of light receiving elements, characteristics of a subject image formed onto the plurality of light receiving elements via the plurality of micro-lenses, wherein: the focus detection unit detects the defocus quantity through a method optimal for the characteristics of the subject image recognized by the recognition unit.

outputs.L1: A focus detection device includes: a plurality of microlenses, arranged in a two-dimensional array, upon which light fluxes passing through an image-forming optical system are incident; a plurality of light-receiving elements disposed in correspondence with each of the plurality of microlenses; a focus detection unit configured to detect a defocus amount of the image-forming optical system by detecting, based on outputs from the plurality of light-receiving elements, a phase difference between a plurality of light fluxes passing through different regions of the image-forming optical system; and a recognition unit configured to recognize, based on the outputs from the plurality of light-receiving elements, characteristics of a subject image formed on the plurality of light-receiving elements via the plurality of microlenses. The focus detection unit detects the defocus amount using a method optimized for the characteristics of the subject image recognized by the recognition unit.
outputs.L2: A focus detection apparatus comprises multiple microlenses arranged in a two-dimensional array to receive light beams passing through an image-forming optical system, and multiple light-receiving elements provided for each microlens. A focus detection section determines the optical system’s amount of defocus by using the outputs of the light-receiving elements to identify phase differences among light beams traveling through separate regions of the optical system. A recognition section analyzes those outputs to determine the characteristics of a subject image projected onto the light-receiving elements through the microlenses. The focus detection section then selects a detection technique suited to the identified subject-image characteristics and uses that technique to calculate the defocus amount.
outputs.L3:
The focus detection device includes a two-dimensional array of micro-lenses that receives light through an image-forming optical system. Each micro-lens in the array corresponds to multiple light-receiving elements, which generate output signals based on the incident light.

A recognition unit analyzes these output signals to identify characteristics of the subject image. Meanwhile, a focus detection unit determines the defocus quantity of the image-forming optical system by detecting phase differences between light fluxes passing through different areas of the optical system. Based on the subject-image characteristics identified by the recognition unit, the focus detection unit selects an appropriate defocus detection method. This adaptive selection enables focus detection to be optimized for the particular subject being imaged.
outputs.L4:
A focus detection device includes a two-dimensional microlens array and a corresponding two-dimensional light-receiver array. Each microlens divides light from an imaging optical system into a plurality of light fluxes and directs those fluxes onto associated light-receiving elements. The device generates multiple image signals representing light that has passed through different regions of the exit pupil of the imaging optical system. By comparing the relative positions, or phase differences, of these image signals, the device calculates the direction and amount of defocus.

Because the light-receiving elements are arranged two-dimensionally, phase differences can be detected in multiple directions and over different regions of the subject image. The device analyzes characteristics of the image formed on the array, such as edge direction, contrast, spatial frequency, pattern repetition, brightness, and the presence of low-texture areas. Based on those characteristics, it selects an appropriate focus-detection direction, signal combination, detection region, or calculation technique. For example, it may use signals aligned perpendicular to a prominent edge, avoid a direction affected by a repetitive pattern, or combine results from several regions when a single region does not provide sufficient reliability.

The selected image signals are then correlated to determine their displacement, and the displacement is converted into a defocus amount for the imaging optical system. Reliability may be evaluated from the sharpness of the correlation result, the signal level, and the consistency of measurements obtained from different directions or regions. Measurements judged unreliable can be rejected or assigned less weight.

By adapting the focus-detection method to the characteristics of the actual subject image, the device reduces errors caused by directional patterns, weak contrast, repetitive textures, noise, and local image irregularities. It therefore provides faster and more accurate defocus measurement across a wide range of subjects and can supply a dependable focus-control signal to an autofocus mechanism.
outputs.L5:
## Focus Detection

Focus detection is the process of determining whether an image, object, or area is sharp and clearly defined. It is widely used in digital cameras, smartphones, microscopes, and computer vision systems. By analyzing contrast, edges, and fine details, a focus detection system can identify blurred areas and adjust the lens or notify the user.

Modern cameras commonly use phase-detection or contrast-detection autofocus. Phase detection is fast and effective for moving subjects, while contrast detection offers high accuracy when the subject is stationary. Many devices combine both methods to improve speed and reliability.

In artificial intelligence applications, focus detection can also refer to identifying the most important region of an image or video. This helps systems prioritize relevant information, improve image quality, and support tasks such as object recognition, medical imaging, and automated inspection.
